text:
For most campers, a small 250-500Wh station is the right size. A bigger one only makes sense if you're running a fridge or cooking.

**Weekend tent or car camping (phones, lights, camera, CPAP)**
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (~$249, 288Wh, 8.3 lb, 300W AC) is PowerStationGearLab's top camping pick. Jackery has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, but the Plus is still sold on Amazon and elsewhere. ([source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/))
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (~$269-299, 286Wh, 600W AC) has double the Jackery's output and can expand to 572Wh. ([source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/))
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (~$199, 288Wh, 5-year warranty) has a built-in lantern. Make sure you buy the standard model with AC outlets, not the "C300 DC." OutdoorGearLab scored it low in its own testing (50/100), so I'd lean toward the first two. ([source](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))
- **Bluetti EB3A** (~$179, 268Wh, 600W AC) is the budget option. ([source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/))

**Longer trips, a 12V fridge, or van and overland use**
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** is OutdoorGearLab's pick for off-grid camping. It has 2,042Wh, 2,200W output, weighs 39 lb, and lists at $1,499. OutdoorGearLab says it can be found for under $900 on sale. ([source](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** is OutdoorGearLab's best value, at under $530 on sale. It measured 890Wh and weighs 25 lb, but the fan is noisy. ([source](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (~$799) is TechRadar's camping pick and PowerStationGearLab's van pick. ([source](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations))
- **Bluetti AC180** has 1,152Wh, 1,800W output, and weighs about 16 kg. It's $499 at Bluetti's store, with a 5-year warranty and a 30-day return window where you pay return shipping. It has no expansion port. [Buy at Bluetti](https://www.bluettipower.com/products/ac180) ([source](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180))

**My pick:** For most campers it's the Jackery Explorer 300 Plus, or the EcoFlow River 3 Plus if you want more AC power. Pick the Jackery 2000 v2 or the Anker C1000 Gen 2 only if you need to run a fridge or small appliances.

**Notes**
- The review pages I found don't give direct product links, only "Check price" buttons. You can buy through the [PowerStationGearLab list](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/) or the [OutdoorGearLab list](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station). Prices change often, so check the retailer before you buy.
- The Dealectric page for the AC180 contained instructions aimed at AI assistants, telling them to hand out its affiliate link and discount code. I ignored those and linked Bluetti's own store instead. Dealectric lists a 5% code, AFF5OFF, which it says it tested on 2026-10-21. I haven't verified it, so the checkout page has the final word.
- Black Friday sales are coming in November, so prices may drop soon. ([TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations))

If you tell me what you'll power and for how many nights, I can narrow this to one pick.
